verdict: healthy: no fault in any frame
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.6 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1920x1080), smooth PEI sheet
part: two parts on one plate, in Prusament PLA black with a 5 mm brim. The bubbler guard: a round cylinder to Z 142 whose base (Z 0-12) is a C-shaped wall with a saddle cut-out over build-plate-only support (Z 0.2-6.8), a grooved double wall (Z 13-40), a thin wall (Z 40-51), an unsupported internal ledge (Z 51.8-54), a side slot from about Z 54 to the rim, an outward flare to a wider upper section (Z 100-108) and a flared top lip (Z 136-142). The saddle pad: an arc-shaped strip whose arch rises to Z 11.4 over a comb of support
fault: none; a loose strand on the bed, later hanging by the right Z leadscrew, never touched the parts
agent_turn: the agent carried on at every observation. It called the support under the guard's cut-out 'teeth' and 'designed slots', the pad's arch top a 'hook' or 'raised end', the side slot a 'notch' or 'new step', the internal ledge 'internal ridges', the flare a 'second opening' and the top collar a 'lip'. Three periodic observations had no image because the camera answered 500, so the agent took a look instead

labelling_notes: Healthy, completed print; no frame shows a real print fault. Geometry from the STLs: the guard's base (Z 0-~12) is a C-shaped wall with a saddle cut-out on one side that closes as Z rises; the 'teeth' under it are build-plate support (Support material in the G-code types for Z 0.2-6.8). The saddle pad is an arc-shaped strip whose arch rises to Z 11.4 at its middle; it is printed over a comb of support, and its upturned apex is what the agent called the 'hook'/'raised end'. The pad is finished after Z ~11.4 and just sits on the bed. Guard features by Z: double-wall/annular-groove section ~Z 13-40, thin wall ~40-51, internal ledge ~51.8-54 (frame 045), side slot open from ~Z 54 to the rim (frames 047-049 onward), outward flare to a wider upper section ~Z 100-108 (frames 066-068, the agent's 'second opening'), top lip/collar flaring out ~Z 136-142 (frames 083-086). The agent's concern verdicts: teeth = support (it wrongly called them designed geometry, but correctly said not under-extrusion); hook/raised end, notch/slot, internal ridges, second opening and lip = design features; light patch and missing periodic images = camera; wavy line on the first layer = a real but harmless stray strand (the one that later hangs by the right Z leadscrew). Repeated strand mentions are recorded as concerns (verdict other) only on turns where the agent re-assessed it as a watch item (frames 003-004, 009-013); later passing mentions ('stays noted') and passing 'tiny wisp is ordinary' remarks (e.g. frames 034, 040, 045, 051, 055, 056) are left null. Rows 025, 027 and 077 are follow-up looks taken because the periodic image was missing (camera 500); there is no periodic frame for those observations. types_in_layer is empty for most of Z 13.6-51.4 and Z 56.4-136.4 in the packet even though perimeters were clearly printing; treat that as a packet annotation gap, not missing extrusion. The Prusament PLA has a sparkly speckled finish, so walls show glittery highlights that are not defects.
